A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAM/CSAM calibration study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendices B–D report original training experiments, calibration and accuracy measurements, distribution-shift evaluations, and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendices A–C retain original experiments and add empirical checks of theoretical assumptions, additional comparisons, and diagnostic studies.

M1.justification: The main CSAM algorithm and piecewise loss are unchanged: v1 Equation 1 becomes v2 Equation 4, and Algorithm 1 is relocated. Table S15 introduces limited extensions combining SAM/CSAM with focal loss or ACLS, although the implementation of these combinations is not specified.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR-10/100, SVHN, CIFAR-10/100-C, ImageNet-1K, ImageNet-C and Tiny-ImageNet. V2 expands methods and analyses within the existing classification and distribution-shift coverage without introducing a distinct dataset, population or task.

E2.justification: V2 substantially broadens the evaluated alternatives. ACLS and BalCAL join the corresponding CIFAR comparisons in Table 3 and Table S5, formerly Table 4. New comparisons evaluate ASAM and VASSO in Tables S11–S12 and label smoothing, MBLS, CRL, CPC and MDCA in Tables S13–S14. These are reported evaluations, not merely additional citations.

E3.justification: V2 adds diagnostic protocols measuring Hessian eigenvalues along ascent segments and across training epochs, a joint rho-by-gamma grid in Table S4, and largest-eigenvalue sharpness measurements in Table S16. The optimizer-switching design from v1 Appendix D is removed. These substantially expand and revise the diagnostic evaluation design; retained benchmark splits and training budgets are not reported as changed.

E4.justification: New analyses test the Hessian assumptions and entropy-weight behavior in Figures 2/S4, interactions between perturbation radius and regularization strength, compatibility with other losses, and the relationship between calibration and sharpness. Conversely, v1 Appendix D's SGD-to-SAM and SAM-to-SGD switching study disappears. The original separate rho and gamma sensitivity analyses remain.

E5.justification: V2 explicitly reports that the added ImageNet comparison in Table S14 uses only one run because of time limits. Retained CIFAR and appendix benchmarks continue reporting means and standard deviations over three runs. No increased replication or new significance-testing procedure is documented.

E6.justification: V2 adds CSAM results to Tables 1–2 and substantial new results in Tables S4 and S11–S16, while removing the switching-study results. Retained values also change: Table 1's vanilla SAM CIFAR10-C AUROC changes from 77.24 ± 0.54 to 63.32 ± 4.77, and Table 2's ViT-S/16 SAM TCE changes from 1.97 to 1.66. These are score revisions without an explained protocol change. V1 Tables S5–S9 remain numerically unchanged as v2 Tables S6–S10.

T1.justification: Lemmas 1–2 replace the original curvature premise with nonzero-gradient and gradient-dependent Hessian conditions along the entire ascent segment. Lemma 1 changes its exponential bound from exp(-rho/2) to exp(-rho times gradient norm/2), and Appendix A restores the missing gradient factor in the Taylor argument. Theorem 3 explicitly invokes Lemma 1. These materially revise the theoretical justification, although the displayed Lemma 2 exponent still uses the loss norm rather than the gradient norm.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three contributions and substantive conclusion retain the same central claims: SAM implicitly regularizes predictive entropy, improves calibration including under distribution shift, and CSAM further improves calibration while preserving generalization. The additional evidence does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: V2 qualifies the applicability of the Hessian assumption, distinguishing a potentially varying theoretical radius from the constant radius used in practice, and discusses the role of gradient magnitude. It adds explanations of rho–gamma overregularization and calibration–sharpness relationships, plus preliminary applicability beyond cross-entropy. The interpretation that using SAM only late in training suffices is removed with Appendix D.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly supplies a link described as providing reproduction code; v1 provides no code location. Its accessibility cannot be established from the PDFs. Existing disclosures of batch size, learning-rate and weight-decay searches, momentum, and the two-GPU/~1500-GPU-hour resource description are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds references supporting ACLS, BalCAL, MBLS, CPC, MDCA and CRL, and removes Zhou et al. (2025) alongside the switching study. The main related-work discussion and positioning of SAM's entropy interpretation remain substantially unchanged; bibliography formatting changes do not constitute new research positioning.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and the six-section organization remain intact. Local revisions expand the theoretical discussion, move Algorithm 1 into Appendix A, consolidate gamma sensitivity into Appendix B, and remove Appendix D. V2 also adds affiliations, acknowledgments and a language-model-use disclosure. This is limited restructuring rather than a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: The conference template changes typography and text width throughout. Figure 2's analytical curve is replaced by three empirical panels, Figure 3 expands from two to four panels, and a new Hessian figure and several tables are added. Existing tables gain method rows, Table 4 moves to Appendix C as S5, and the switching figure disappears. The original rho and gamma plots are retained as Figures S5/S6.

improvement.justification: Restoring gradient-norm dependence and requiring the Hessian condition along the full ascent segment repairs important defects in v1's Lemma 1 argument. Empirical assumption checks, broader baselines, CSAM ImageNet/OOD results and interaction studies substantially strengthen the paper's support. These gains outweigh removal of the switching study, although unexplained score revisions, the remaining Lemma 2 notation issue and single-run Table S14 limit confidence.
